maml:description.maml:para: Registers a Windows Update service.

Registers an update service with the Windows Update Agent so that searches can use it. The cmdlet has four ways to name the service: by ID with -ServiceID, Microsoft Update with -MicrosoftUpdate, a service on a remote computer with -ComputerName, or an offline scan package (wsusscn2.cab) with -ScanFileLocation. It restarts the Windows Update service before and after the registration.
The cmdlet combines the old Add-WUServiceManager and Add-WUOfflineSync functions. Registered services appear in Get-WUServiceManager and can be used with the -ServiceID, -MicrosoftUpdate, and -WindowsUpdate parameters of Get-WindowsUpdate.

Specifies how the service is registered, as a combination of these values: 1 (asfAllowPendingRegistration), 2 (asfAllowOnlineRegistration), and 4 (asfRegisterServiceWithAU). The default value 2 allows online registration.

Specifies the path of the Microsoft-signed cabinet file (.cab) that has the information required to register the service. If you omit it, the Windows Update Agent looks for the authorization cabinet file when a network connection is available.

Specifies one or more computers on which to register the service. The default is the local computer. Available in the RemoteServiceID and MicrosoftUpdate parameter sets. Accepts pipeline input by value and by property name.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

Specifies the email settings used by -SendReport, as a hashtable. SmtpServer, From, and To are required. Properties is an array of property names to include, '*' for every property of the first result object, or '**' for every property of every result object. Style is Table or List. Keys that you do not supply are read from PSWUSettings.xml in the module folder (see Set-PSWUSettings). The SMTP credential is read from Windows Credential Manager.
Specifies the path of the offline scan file (wsusscan.cab or wsusscn2.cab) to register as an update service.

Sends the results by email when the cmdlet finishes. The SMTP settings come from -PSWUSettings or from the PSWUSettings.xml file saved by Set-PSWUSettings. If the settings are incomplete, an error is written and no report is sent.

Specifies the ID (GUID) of the service to register. Examples: Windows Update 9482f4b4-e343-43b6-b170-9a65bc822c77, Microsoft Update 7971f918-a847-4430-9279-4a52d1efe18d, Windows Store 117cab2d-82b1-4b5a-a08c-4d62dbee7782, Windows Server Update Service 3da21691-e39d-4da6-8a4b-b43877bcb1b7.

maml:alert.maml:para: This cmdlet requires an elevated session and stops with an error when the session is not elevated. -WhatIf and -Confirm are accepted but the cmdlet does not check them, so the changes are always made. maml:description.maml:para: Gets the updates that match your criteria and optionally downloads, installs, hides, or unhides them.

Searches a Windows Update service for updates that match the criteria you give and returns them. With no action switch the cmdlet only lists the updates. Add -Download, -Install, or -Hide, or call one of the aliases, to act on the updates it found.
The aliases select an action: - Install-WindowsUpdate is the same as -Download -Install. - Download-WindowsUpdate is the same as -Download. - Hide-WindowsUpdate is the same as -Hide. - Show-WindowsUpdate and UnHide-WindowsUpdate are the same as -Hide:$false, and they include hidden updates in the search. - Get-WUList and Get-WUInstall do not select an action. Get-WUInstall does not install anything unless you add -Install.
Updates are filtered in two stages. Pre-search criteria are sent to the Windows Update service and evaluated there: -Criteria, -UpdateType, -DeploymentAction, -IsAssigned, -IsPresent, -BrowseOnly, -AutoSelectOnWebSites, -UpdateID, -NotUpdateID, -RevisionNumber, -CategoryIDs, -IsInstalled, -IsHidden, and -WithHidden. When you use -Criteria, it replaces the query that the other pre-search parameters would build. Post-search criteria are applied on the computer to the pre-filtered list: -RootCategories, -Category, -NotCategory, -KBArticleID, -NotKBArticleID, -Title, -NotTitle, -Severity, -NotSeverity, -MaxSize, -MinSize, -IgnoreUserInput, -IgnoreRebootRequired, and -AutoSelectOnly. Use -ShowPreSearchCriteria to see the query that was sent.
By default the cmdlet asks for confirmation for each update before it downloads, installs, hides, or unhides it. Use -AcceptAll to skip the prompts. Without -WindowsUpdate, -MicrosoftUpdate, or -ServiceID the search uses the default Automatic Updates service of the computer (for example a WSUS server).
On a remote computer only the search runs interactively. To download or install, or when you use -ScheduleJob, the cmdlet registers a scheduled task through Invoke-WUJob that runs Get-WindowsUpdate -AcceptAll on the target, because the Windows Update Agent does not allow remote downloads and installations. The module must be installed on the target, and the task writes its output to PSWindowsUpdateNext.log in the TEMP folder of the SYSTEM account.
The Status property is a seven-character string: - Position 1: A for an accepted update, R for a rejected update, or - when no action was requested. - Position 2: D if the update is downloaded, F if its download failed, - if it is not downloaded, ? if the download runs in a scheduled task. - Position 3: I if the update is installed, R if it was installed and needs a restart, F if the installation failed, - if it is not installed, ? if the installation runs in a scheduled task. - Position 4: M for a mandatory update. - Position 5: H for a hidden update. - Position 6: U for an uninstallable update. - Position 7: B for a beta update. A flag that does not apply is shown as -. After -Hide or -Hide:$false, the string has only positions 2 to 7.
Accepts every update that matches the criteria without asking for confirmation. It applies to download, installation, hide, and unhide.
Restarts the computer without asking when a restart is required after an installation.
Post-search criteria. Keeps only the updates that Windows Update flags to be selected automatically (AutoSelectOnWebSites) and accepts them without asking.

Pre-search criteria. -AutoSelectOnWebSites finds updates that Windows Update flags to be selected automatically. -AutoSelectOnWebSites:$false finds updates that are not flagged. The criterion is added only when you specify the parameter.
Pre-search criteria. -BrowseOnly finds updates that are considered optional. -BrowseOnly:$false finds updates that are not optional. The criterion is added only when you specify the parameter.

Specifies one or more computers to run against. The default is the local computer. Searching works interactively on remote computers through DCOM. Downloading and installing register a scheduled task through Invoke-WUJob instead. Accepts pipeline input by value and by property name.

After updates are installed, sends the update history (Get-WUHistory) by email through a scheduled task. If a restart is required, the report is sent after the next startup. Requires the email settings described under -SendReport.

Sends the results by email when the cmdlet finishes. The SMTP settings come from -PSWUSettings or from the PSWUSettings.xml file saved by Set-PSWUSettings. The default properties are ComputerName, Status, KB, Size, and Title.

Examples: Windows Update 9482f4b4-e343-43b6-b170-9a65bc822c77, Microsoft Update 7971f918-a847-4430-9279-4a52d1efe18d, Windows Store 117cab2d-82b1-4b5a-a08c-4d62dbee7782, Windows Server Update Service 3da21691-e39d-4da6-8a4b-b43877bcb1b7.

Writes the query that is sent to the update service to the host. It shows only the pre-search criteria.
Post-search criteria. Finds updates whose title matches this regular expression, for example '.NET Framework 4'. The match is not case sensitive.
Pre-search criteria. Finds updates with these update IDs (GUIDs), for example 12345678-9abc-def0-1234-56789abcdef0. When you pass several IDs, an update that matches any of them is found.
Pre-search criteria. Finds updates of one type: Driver or Software. By default all types are found.

Searches the public Windows Update service (ServiceID 9482f4b4-e343-43b6-b170-9a65bc822c77) and ignores a configured WSUS server.

maml:description.maml:para: Downloads update packages from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

Searches the Microsoft Update Catalog (catalog.update.microsoft.com) for a KB article, lists the catalog entries it finds, and downloads every file of the entries you accept. Use it to get .msu and .cab packages for computers that cannot reach Windows Update. The cmdlet asks for confirmation for each entry unless you use -AcceptAll; use -UpdateID to limit the search to chosen entries.
The cmdlet first returns every catalog entry it considered, with Result set to Accepted, Rejected, or Error. Error means the Catalog listed no files for the entry. After the downloads, it returns only the entries whose files all downloaded and passed verification, with Result set to Downloaded. Entries that were canceled or failed are not returned a second time; their errors and warnings explain why. The Files property lists every file of an entry with its Url, FileName, and Digest. After the download it also has SignatureStatus, SignerSubject, Path, and Sha256.
Files are downloaded with BITS into -Destination, which is created if it does not exist; existing files with the same name are overwritten. Only HTTPS URLs on windowsupdate.com or microsoft.com hosts are accepted. Each file is checked against the SHA-1 digest that the Catalog publishes, and its Authenticode signature is verified. A file that fails the digest check is deleted. A file whose signature fails verification, is revoked, or does not chain to a Microsoft root is also deleted, unless you use -SkipSignatureCheck. If revocation cannot be checked, for example because the computer is offline or behind a proxy, a file that matched the Catalog digest is kept and a warning is written.
Downloads every catalog entry that matches without asking for confirmation.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Specifies the folder to download the files to. The folder is created if it does not exist. Existing files with the same name are overwritten.
Specifies the KB article number to search for, with or without the KB prefix, for example KB5034123 or 5034123. Accepts pipeline input by value and by property name.

Keeps downloaded files whose Authenticode signature fails verification or does not chain to a Microsoft root, instead of deleting them. A warning is written for each file that is kept. The SHA-1 digest check still applies: a file that does not match the digest published by the Catalog is always deleted. Use this switch only for packages that you have verified in another way.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs a PowerShell script on local or remote computers through a Task Scheduler job.

The task runs as SYSTEM with the highest privileges. It starts powershell.exe with -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand, so quotation marks in -Script cannot change the command line; the readable script is stored in the task description. The task is hidden by default. Its trigger expires (see -EndBoundary), and Task Scheduler deletes the task 30 minutes after that.
Because the script cannot interact with a user, use -AcceptAll with Install-WindowsUpdate. By default the script is: ipmo PSWindowsUpdateNext; Get-WindowsUpdate -AcceptAll -Install | Out-File $Env:TEMP\PSWindowsUpdateNext.log

maml:description.maml:para: Resets the Windows Update components on the local computer.

Resets the Windows Update client to a clean state in ten steps: it stops the BITS, Windows Update, Application Identity, and Cryptographic Services services; deletes the BITS queue files (qmgr*.dat); renames the SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 folders to .bak copies; deletes the old WindowsUpdate.log; resets the BITS and Windows Update service security descriptors; re-registers the related DLLs in System32 with regsvr32, skipping any that are not present; resets Winsock and the WinHTTP proxy with netsh; restarts the services; and asks the agent to re-detect updates (wuauclt /resetauthorization /detectnow).

maml:description.maml:para: Saves the email settings that PSWindowsUpdateNext uses for reports.

Stores the SMTP settings used by the -SendReport parameter of the other cmdlets. Server, port, SSL, recipient, sender, subject, properties, and style are saved in PSWUSettings.xml in the module folder (next to PSWindowsUpdateNext.psd1). Only the settings you specify are changed; the others keep their values.
A credential given with -SmtpCredential is saved in Windows Credential Manager under the target PSWindowsUpdateNext. Scheduled tasks run as SYSTEM, which has its own Credential Manager, so the cmdlet also registers a short-lived task through Invoke-WUJob that saves the credential for SYSTEM. The password is passed to that task protected with DPAPI (machine scope) through -SaveAsSystem.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Specifies a user account that has permission to register the task that saves the SMTP credential for SYSTEM. The default is the current user.
Returns the original exception instead of the module's short error message when an operation fails. Set $DebugPreference to 'Continue' for more diagnostic output.

Specifies which properties of the result objects the report contains and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml. Use '*' for all properties of the first object or '**' for all properties of all objects. To report a list of property names, pass a Properties array in the -PSWUSettings hashtable of the cmdlet that sends the report.

Used internally. Contains the SMTP credential, protected with DPAPI for the local computer, that the task registered by this cmdlet stores in the Credential Manager of the SYSTEM account. Do not set it yourself.
Sends the saved settings by email as a test report after they are saved.
Specifies the credential for the SMTP server and saves it in Windows Credential Manager, for the current user and for SYSTEM.
Specifies whether to use SSL to connect to the SMTP server and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml. Pass a Boolean value, for example -SmtpEnableSsl $true.
Specifies the sender address and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml.
Specifies the SMTP port and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml. The default is 25.
Specifies the SMTP server and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml.
Specifies the subject of the report email and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml. If you do not set a subject, reports use the computer name, the text 'Windows Update report', and the date.
Specifies the recipient address and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml.
Specifies how the report presents the results, Table or List, and saves it in PSWUSettings.xml.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
A collection with one object per computer that shows the settings that were saved.

maml:alert.maml:para: The cmdlet writes a warning when the session is not elevated. -WhatIf and -Confirm are accepted but the cmdlet does not check them, so the settings are always saved. The ComputerName parameter is not available on this cmdlet in the current release; it always saves the settings on the local computer. Email reports use System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient, which Microsoft recommends against for new development.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 1: Use Microsoft 365 as the SMTP server ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```powershell Set-PSWUSettings -SmtpServer smtp.office365.com -SmtpPort 587 -SmtpEnableSsl $true -SmtpSubject 'Windows Update report' -SmtpTo admins@contoso.com -SmtpFrom wu-reports@contoso.com -SmtpCredential (Get-Credential wu-reports@contoso.com) ```
Saves the settings and the credential. Cmdlets that you run later with -SendReport use them.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 2: Include every property and use the list layout ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```powershell Set-PSWUSettings -Properties '**' -Style List ```

maml:description.maml:para: Sets the Windows Update client policy settings.

Writes Windows Update policy values to the registry on the local or a remote computer, under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate and its AU subkey. The keys are created if they do not exist. Most parameters write the registry value that has the same name; -NotificationLevel writes AUOptions. Get-WUSettings reads the same values.
Only the settings you specify are changed. A switch parameter such as -NoAutoUpdate writes 1; -NoAutoUpdate:$false writes 0. Many policies come in pairs: a Set... or ...Enabled switch turns the policy on, and a second parameter holds its value, for example -SetActiveHours with -ActiveHoursStart and -ActiveHoursEnd.
Group Policy overrides these values on the next policy refresh. The cmdlet reports the settings that it changed.
Enabled - The WSUS server distributes available signed non-Microsoft updates.
Disabled - The WSUS server does not distribute available signed non-Microsoft updates.

maml:description.maml:para: Installs or updates PSWindowsUpdateNext on remote computers.

Deploys the module to other computers so that remote operations such as Invoke-WUJob can run there. With -Online, the cmdlet runs Install-Module -Name PSWindowsUpdateNext -Force on the remote computer through PowerShell remoting, after it installs the NuGet package provider. The module must be available in the PowerShell Gallery. With -Local, the cmdlet copies the newest installed copy of the module on this computer to the same path on the remote computer over the administrative share (\\computer\C$\...) and then runs Enable-WURemoting there.
The cmdlet reports the remote module version before and after the update in the verbose stream.
Specifies one or more computers to update. With -Online the default is the local computer; with -Local the parameter is required. Accepts pipeline input by value and by property name.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Specifies a user account that has permission to update the module on the computers. The default is the current user.
Returns the original exception instead of the module's short error message when an operation fails. Set $DebugPreference to 'Continue' for more diagnostic output.
Copies the module from this computer to the remote computer over the administrative share. Requires SMB access to the destination.
Installs the module from the PowerShell Gallery. This is the default parameter set.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
You can pipe computer names to ComputerName.
The verbose and error records of the remote command.

maml:alert.maml:para: The cmdlet has a confirmation impact of High, so it asks for confirmation. Remoting uses Negotiate authentication. With -Local, Enable-WURemoting changes firewall rules and remoting settings on the remote computer; see its notes.
